stem: A child in a remote hospital has a painful irreducible inguinal hernia and no local paediatric surgeon. What is the best management?

options.text: Discharge and review in one week
Apply a truss and observe at home
Provide analgesia, keep fasting and arrange urgent transfer to paediatric surgery
Perform routine outpatient ultrasound before referral

explanation: An irreducible inguinal hernia is an urgent surgical problem. The child needs analgesia, fasting status and urgent transfer or consultation with paediatric surgery when local expertise is unavailable.
rationale: An irreducible inguinal hernia is an urgent surgical problem. The child needs analgesia, fasting status and urgent transfer or consultation with paediatric surgery when local expertise is unavailable.

options.text: Give analgesia, make an appointment for paeds clinic tomorrow
Give analgesia, refer to adult surgeons in the town
Give analgesia and transfer to a paediatric surgery facility
